title: Ways to find work
reading: You have several options when you are looking for a job in Norway:
use your network internet: nav.no and finn.no temping agencies
Many employers think that references are important. They can then ask previous employers about how the applicant performs at work. A former boss or colleague can give good references.

Finding a job for the first time in Norway can be difficult because people may not have references or an extensive network. It may therefore be a good idea to do practical training in a workplace for a period, take some courses etc. Practical training and various odd jobs enable you to develop your network and obtain references.

It is said that between 60 and 80 per cent of jobs in Norway are not advertised, but are filled through people’s networks. Your network is all the people you know, meet and are in contact with. Your network can include family, relations, friends, acquaintances, colleagues, neighbours, teachers and case officers.
discussion: Talk together How do people normally go about finding a job in your home country? Talk about different ways of finding work in Norway. Who was in your network before you came to Norway? Who is in your network now? Do you need a bigger network in Norway? How are you going to go about expanding it?
exercises: Select the right answer What is a reference? When friends describe what kind of person you are and what you like to do in your spare time. When previous bosses or colleagues describe how the applicant has functioned in the job. When the family describes what kind of role you have in the family, and what you are good at. Select the right answer What is a network? Everyone in our neighbourhood and their families and friends. Everyone we know, meet and are in contact with. Everyone who lives in and around the city we live in. Select the right answer Is it common to advertise vacant positions in Norway? Yes, all workplaces in Norway are obliged by law to advertise all vacant positions. No, between 60 and 80 per cent of vacant positions are not advertised. No, only 1 in 10 vacant positions are advertised.
